items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: we had a good little band with Eddie Hayward and Vic Dickenson... Ernie Shepherd (PHONETIC) was the bass player

ctx.x: Was that your first trip to New York?

Not really, I'd gone -- as a player, yes. I'd gone there as a visitor before, but not as a playing musician. It was my first trip to New York and after that, it was all go. From then on, with the exception of about five years that I spent at home here, after I left Eddie Hayward's (PHONETIC) band, which I joined when I left out of service, we had a good little band with Eddie Hayward and Vic Dickenson. Henry Coker (PHONETIC) played trombones. A fellow by the name of Par Jones (PHONETIC) played trumpet and I…

I went back to New York with them at the end of '45, when I got out of service. I left Eddie Hayward in April, 1946, came back home and I stayed home without leaving until I went with the Basie Band in January of '51. I didn't want to go nowhere. But after I left with the Basie Band, I never set down anymore until 1970. It was all go. We entertained,
